Darth Sion — Legends feat/statement extraction
Article: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Darth_Sion
Scope: Main article text reviewed through “Notes and references” and the end of the article. Navigation, appearances, source lists, and trivia without a feat are omitted. Character opinions/hype are marked as statements, not feats. Bracketed numbers are the article's citations.

[Lead / summary]

- “Rather than die, though, Sion found that by calling on his pain, anger, and hatred, he could rise from certain death and achieve immortality, at the cost of all-consuming agony.” [Statement of ability/feat; cited 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: “With a body fractured and decomposing, held together only by the dark side of the Force, Sion survived the Great Sith War.”
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Sion" rev 15650112 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

- “With a body fractured and decomposing, held together only by the dark side of the Force, Sion survived the Great Sith War.” [Concrete survival feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: His immortality is attributed to pain, anger, hatred, and the dark side; no opponent comparison is made here.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Sion" rev 15650112 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

- “Eventually, frustrated with her teachings, he and Nihilus stripped her of the Force and cast her out.” [Concrete feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Sion did this together with Darth Nihilus against Darth Traya.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Sion" rev 15650112 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

- “With the Jedi all but eliminated, Sion took notice of a new Jedi returning to known space, the Jedi Knight Meetra Surik, who had been exiled since the Mandalorian Wars.” [Outcome attributed to the Sith campaign; not a solo feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article states that Sion and Nihilus continued the war on the Jedi and that the Jedi were all but eliminated.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Sion" rev 15650112 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

- “Sion awaited Surik on Malachor V; in their final battle he was struck down again and again, but rose each time.” [Concrete regeneration/resurrection feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The repeated defeats are in Sion's final battle with Meetra Surik.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Sion" rev 15650112 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

[Biography — Rise of a Sith Lord]

- “In the Great Sith War of 3996 BBY, Sion served as a Sith Marauder in Exar Kun's Sith Empire.” [Contextual statement]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: He served under Exar Kun's Sith Empire.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Seeking death, Sion went into battle against the Jedi but continued to survive the encounters.” [Concrete survival feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The opponents named are Jedi; the article does not identify their individual ranks here.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Eventually, Sion was struck down, but he did not die.” [Concrete durability/immortality feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: This follows his repeated survival against Jedi.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Instead, the pain within him welled up to agonizing levels, driving Sion to rise once more and strike down his would-be killer with all his anger and hate.” [Concrete resurrection and kill feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The killer is the person who had struck Sion down; no further scaling is stated.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Sion found that he could hold his own decomposing body together with the dark side of the Force.” [Concrete Force ability]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The same paragraph says the process caused excruciating pain and required continuous concentration on rage.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Kun ultimately lost the war, but Sion survived the fall of Kun's Empire.” [Concrete survival feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Sion survived the collapse of Exar Kun's empire; no direct power comparison is stated.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Kreia would later claim that Sion was ‘spawned by the horrors’ of this war.” [Character statement, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Kreia's statement refers to the Mandalorian Wars.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion was at the Sith Academy on Korriban in its final days, and he watched as the Sith turned on each other. Sion survived this bout of backstabbing, though.” [Concrete survival feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The survival is during the collapse of Revan's Sith Empire.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords ; Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4,2; exact text match]

[Biography — The Sith Triumvirate]

- “Sion, Traya, and Nihilus allied into the secretive Sith Triumvirate, based out of Malachor V, their goal was the annihilation of the Jedi Order and restoration of the Sith to power.” [Goal/setting statement; cited 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Sion is grouped with Darth Traya and Darth Nihilus in the Triumvirate.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “At Trayus Academy, a hidden Sith stronghold on Malachor V, Sion learned more of pain.” [Training statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Trayus Academy is identified as a hidden Sith stronghold.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “While Traya meditated in the academy's core, Sion and Nihilus closed in on her. Sion beat her mercilessly, the two sapped her energy before Nihilus stripped her of the Force, and Traya was cast out.” [Concrete combat/overthrow feat; cited 4, 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The feat is shared with Nihilus; Nihilus is specifically credited with stripping Traya of the Force.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords ; Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4,2; exact text match]

- “Relying heavily on the Malachor-based Sith assassins, originally founded by Revan, Sion went on a spree of Jedi assassination.” [Concrete campaign statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The assassins were originally founded by Revan.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “He was killed a number of times over the course of it, but he continued to rise again and slaughter many Jedi in return.” [Concrete resurrection and combat feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The kills occurred during Sion's campaign against Jedi; the article gives no individual Jedi scaling here.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “By the end of Sion's campaign, the Jedi were almost entirely extinct.” [Campaign outcome; not presented as a solo feat]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article directly connects this outcome to Sion's campaign, while also describing the assassins and the wider Sith effort.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “In 3954 BBY, Sion and Nihilus united the majority of the Sith Empire remnants, becoming the most unified force of Sith in their time.” [Political/military feat; cited 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article calls their united remnants “the most unified force of Sith in their time.”
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Lonna Vash, a Master of the Jedi Council, came to Korriban in search of Sion, but she fell into a trap of his and was captured. Sion imprisoned Vash in the abandoned Sith Academy.” [Concrete tactical feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The target is explicitly identified as a Jedi Council Master.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

[Biography — The last of the Jedi]

- “And now you run in search of the Jedi. They are all dead, save one—and one broken Jedi cannot stop the darkness that is to come.” —Sion, to Kreia [Character statement, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Sion characterizes Meetra Surik as the one remaining and “broken” Jedi; this is his claim, not an objective narrator statement.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Rumor that Surik was the last of the Jedi was enough to draw the Sith out of hiding; Sion studied her, where she had gone in her exile, and the battles she had fought in the war.” [Concrete intelligence-gathering statement]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The information concerned Surik's exile and wartime battles.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion's warship intercepted the Hawk and opened fire on it, but the Hawk managed to send out a distress signal.” [Concrete attack statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The target was Kreia's Ebon Hawk.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “The warship, however, played dead, and the Harbinger connected an umbilical to it. The crew found Sion's body, and believing him to be a corpse, took him back to their vessel. Meanwhile, Sion's cloaked assassins infiltrated their way into the Harbinger.” [Concrete infiltration/tactical feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The deception worked on the Harbinger's crew and enabled the assassins' infiltration.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion at last awoke and, after tormenting the mind of a passing crew member, burst from his kolto tank and announced that he had come for Surik.” [Concrete recovery/Force feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article places this after a medical officer could not determine whether he was alive or dead because of his fractures and scars.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “His assassins materialized around him, and they quickly killed the security team sent to medbay.” [Concrete combat outcome; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The action is attributed to Sion's assassins, not solely to Sion.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion at last seized control of the ship, which due to the sabotage of one of its passengers was experiencing a system failure, and opened fire on the Hawk as it fled, hitting it as it leapt into hyperspace.” [Concrete tactical/attack feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The ship was the Harbinger and the target was the Ebon Hawk.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion followed them to the mining world of Peragus II, controlling the Harbinger from a meditative pose on its bridge.” [Concrete control feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article states he controlled the Harbinger while meditating.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Kreia, hiding, leapt out to attack, and Sion wheeled on her and cut off her hand.” [Concrete combat feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The opponent was Kreia; the article does not give a further comparative ranking here.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion pursued in the Harbinger, and the ensuing firefight set off the volatile asteroids around Peragus, consuming the Harbinger in an explosion. Sion survived.” [Concrete survival feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: He survived the destruction of the Harbinger in the Peragus asteroid explosion.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

[Biography — Encounter on Korriban]

- “Did you come here for answers? There are none. The call of Korriban is strong, but it is the call of the dead.” —Darth Sion, to Meetra Surik [Character statement, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: This is Sion's statement to Surik about Korriban.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Shortly after Surik arrived on Korriban, Sion killed the imprisoned Jedi Master.” [Concrete kill feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The victim is explicitly a Jedi Master, Lonna Vash.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion sensed her arrival and had the doors to the Academy sealed behind her, as he sent his assassins in pursuit of her and her companions.” [Concrete sensing/tactical feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The target was Surik and her companions inside the Sith Academy.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “They fought, but even as Surik injured Sion, he called upon the Force to restore his health.” [Concrete regeneration feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Surik is the opponent and is explicitly said to have injured him.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Surik fled the Academy, and Sion, feeling a measure of respect for her, let her go, ordering his assassins not to harm her.” [Concrete tactical decision; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article connects his decision to his respect for Surik.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “The Sith Lord found her beautiful, but he saw in these feelings weakness that would only lead to death.” [Character belief, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article says his feelings reduced his hatred and threatened his life.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

[Biography — The final death]

- “After eliminating Sion's assassins, Traya found him in the Trayus Core.” [Concrete feat by Traya, not Sion's feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Traya is stated to have eliminated Sion's assassins before finding him.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “He considered himself to have come further than any of her former apprentices, including Revan, and had decided that his initial betrayal was a test that he had passed.” [Sion's self-assessment, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Sion explicitly compares himself with Traya's former apprentices, including Revan.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Eventually she came to Malachor in search of Kreia, and after fighting her way through the Sith forces of the academy, Surik at last came face to face with Sion.” [Contextual combat statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Surik fought through the academy's Sith forces before reaching Sion.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Surik struck down Sion, but with the dark power of Malachor flowing through him, he rose again.” [Concrete resurrection feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article attributes the recovery to Malachor's dark power flowing through him.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords ; Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4,2; exact text match]

- “Once more they fought, and once more he fell; Surik tried to persuade Sion that Kreia did not respect him and was using him as a tool, but Sion claimed that if he killed Surik, Traya would have to complete his training as her true apprentice.” [Concrete repeated-defeat statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The fight is against Meetra Surik.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords ; Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4,2; exact text match]

- “As she struck him down a fourth time, Sion remained defiant.” [Concrete repeated-defeat statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article explicitly counts at least four knockdowns by Surik.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords ; Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4,2; exact text match]

- “Finally at peace, and glad to leave the living world behind him at last, Sion allowed himself to die, his body surrendering to absolute necrosis.” [Concrete final-death statement; cited 4, 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: His death follows Surik convincing him to release his hold on his body, hate, and the Force.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords ; Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4,2; exact text match]

[Personality and traits]

- “From his very beginning, Darth Sion filled himself with hatred, ultimately giving him the power to overcome death.” [Characterization/ability statement; cited 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Hatred is identified as the source of his ability to overcome death.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Sion fed upon his pain for sustenance, and he sought to spread it to all Jedi across the galaxy.” [Ability/motive statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article connects his sustenance to pain and his target to Jedi across the galaxy.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion was tenacious; when he cornered his prey on Peragus II, the Sith Lord would not let them go without bloodshed.” [Character assessment with concrete conduct; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The conduct occurred while pursuing prey on Peragus II.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “He was cunning; though Jedi Master Lonna Vash considered him volatile and thought him an easily-influenced brute, Sion would ultimately trap and kill her.” [Concrete tactical/kill feat plus character opinion; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Vash is explicitly identified as a Jedi Master; her “volatile”/“easily-influenced brute” view is marked as her opinion.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Ambitious and power-hungry as well, Sion would not forever bend to the will of his Sith Master, Darth Traya, and he and Darth Nihilus eventually turned on her, using Nihilus' special techniques in the Force to tear down her defenses and then beating her mercilessly.” [Concrete overthrow feat plus characterization; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The feat is shared with Nihilus, and the special Force techniques are attributed to Nihilus.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “While Sion immersed himself in hate, he was still able to feel positive emotions, such as love and compassion, which he felt toward Surik.” [Character statement, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article says these feelings reduced his hatred and endangered his life.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

[Personality and traits — Injuries]

- “In his years as a Sith Marauder, Sion regularly fought on the front lines of the Great Sith War, and in surviving, he built up a tolerance to pain.” [Concrete survival/endurance statement]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article links the tolerance to surviving front-line fighting in the Great Sith War.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “When at last he achieved his method of immortality, every centimeter of Sion's body crawled with agony.” [Condition/ability statement]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The agony is the cost of his method of immortality.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Sion's flesh was decomposing, covered in cracks and scars, and his body existed in a state of undeath.” [Physical-condition statement; cited 2, 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: His undeath is connected to his immortality method.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide ; Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2,4; exact text match]

- “His skeleton was fractured in thousands of places, as every bone in his body had been splintered repeatedly and then reassembled.” [Concrete durability/injury statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article describes the damage as affecting every bone.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “The Force was all that held him together.” [Ability statement; cited 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article attributes his continued physical existence entirely to the Force.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Sion's horrific disfigurements were mentioned by Darth Plagueis to his apprentice, Sidious, when the latter asked if he would be physically transformed by the dark side.” [Cited cross-character statement; cited 10]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Darth Plagueis used Sion's disfigurements as the example in a discussion with Sidious.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 10; exact text match]

[Personal relationships — Kreia]

- “He cannot kill what he cannot see, and power has blinded him long ago.” —Kreia, on the metaphorical eye of Sion [Character opinion, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Kreia's statement characterizes Sion's power as blinding him; it is not an objective power ranking.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Kreia, in turn, believed that Sion's power had blinded him.” [Character opinion, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: This repeats Kreia's assessment of Sion rather than establishing an independent feat.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “She believed his continued existence was a threat to life itself.” [Character opinion/hype, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The claim is Kreia's belief about Sion's continued existence.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

[Personal relationships — Meetra Surik]

- “I hate you because you crawl within my head as she does, but your presence holds no thoughts, no teachings, you are just…there, unspoken. I hate you because you are beautiful to me. And in that weakness lies death.” —Sion, to Meetra Surik [Character statement, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Sion says his feelings for Surik weaken his hold on life.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “When he first set after her, Sion thought Surik to be broken and incapable of stopping the onslaught of the Sith.” [Sion's opinion, not a feat; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: This is Sion's initial assessment of Surik.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Yet, when she bested him in combat, he let her go, believing she had earned it and knowing they would meet again.” [Concrete combat outcome; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Surik is explicitly said to have bested Sion in combat.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Sion" rev 15650112 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

- “However she chose to battle him, defeating him physically several times, however their true battle was mental.” [Concrete repeated-defeat statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article distinguishes Surik's physical victories from the mental aspect of the confrontation.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

[Powers and abilities]

- “As a Sith Lord, Sion learned to use the dark side at Revan's Sith Academy on Korriban, and later learned of the ways of pain at Trayus Academy on Malachor V.” [Training statement; cited 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: His training locations are Revan's Sith Academy and Trayus Academy.
  Source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 4; exact text match]

- “Sion had a number of Force powers at his disposal: Telekinesis ranging from Force Whirlwind to Force Wound, Force Slow, Force rage, Force Immunity, and Force drain.” [Powers list; cited 2, 4]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article gives no comparative scaling for the listed powers.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide ; Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2,4; exact text match]

- “He was also immune to the effects of fear-based Force attacks.” [Concrete resistance feat; cited 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The immunity is specifically to fear-based Force attacks.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Among the powers Sion possessed was his ability to use his hatred to channel the dark side to hold his broken and decayed body together.” [Concrete Force ability]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The ability is directly tied to his hatred and the dark side.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “Though this essentially made him immortal, using it caused Sion to feel excruciating pain as his body had suffered countless injuries that never healed.” [Ability/cost statement]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: The article explicitly calls the result “essentially” immortality and links it to unhealed injuries.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]

- “When struck down, Sion could call upon his anger, hate, and pain to come alive again.” [Concrete resurrection ability; cited 2]
  Scaling connection stated by the article: Anger, hate, and pain are the stated triggers.
  Source: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Sion" rev 15650112, ref 2; exact text match]
